# Intake Brief: Automated Balancing

> **Headline:** Turn the existing same-seed evaluation harness into an
> automated-balancing framework that simulates hundreds of deterministic bot
> games against the real balance data files and reports full statistics, so
> tuning is driven by evidence instead of intuition.

**Priority:** medium · **Issue type:** epic · **Assignee:** Map

## Problem statement

Balancing the game is currently a manual, point-in-time activity: a designer
edits `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` / `ship-config.csv` / `difficulty-curves.csv`,
reloads, watches a run, and guesses. The pieces to do better already exist — a
deterministic headless arena (`src/ai/eval/arena.ts`), a metric/A-B layer
(`src/ai/eval/metrics.ts`), and a telemetry schema that already records
minerals, upgrades (`choice_selected`), kills (`enemy_killed`) and pickups —
but the arena is **not config-driven** (it hardcodes `scout/diver/phaser`, a
fixed fire cadence and radius), the metric layer does **not** aggregate
per-upgrade or per-archetype statistics, and there is no way to run a **batch
of hundreds of games** and read its aggregated distribution. We need a
framework that simulates many bot games, collects full balance statistics, and
reports them so balance can be tuned from evidence rather than intuition.

## Users

- **As a game designer / maintainer**, I want to run hundreds of bot games
  after changing a balance value and get a statistical report (minerals,
  upgrades, kills, survival, wave reached), so I can see whether the change
  improved or hurt play before shipping it.
- **As the bot maintainer**, I want the simulated scenario to read the real
  balance data files, so a run reflects the tuning I just made (not a
  hardcoded copy).
- **As a producer**, I want a stable, reproducible artifact per batch, so a
  balance change can be reviewed and compared over time.
- **As a downstream consumer** (the human-play stats and periodic
  human-experience validation work items), I want one shared balance-statistics
  schema, so bot and human measurements are directly comparable.

## Acceptance criteria
- **Config-driven simulation.** A headless run consumes the real balance data (`src/data/enemy-configs.csv`, `src/data/ship-config.csv`, `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` and/or the shared wave sequencer) through the existing config loaders, with no divergent copy of enemy/ship/wave stats. A test demonstrates that changing a CSV value changes the simulated outcome (e.g. enemy health/`shotProbability`).
- **Batch runner.** A documented command runs at least ~100 deterministic bot games (seeds × policy) in one invocation and completes in a practical time on a dev machine, emitting raw telemetry plus an aggregated report. Same seed + config + policy yields a byte-identical report.
- **Full balance statistics.** The report captures, per run and aggregated, at minimum: minerals collected, upgrades selected (per upgrade/choice id), enemies killed **per archetype**, asteroids destroyed, power-ups collected, avoidable hits, survival time, and wave/level reached — with distribution summaries (count, mean, median, min, max, std-dev) across games.
- **Human-readable + machine-readable output.** The batch writes stable JSON artifacts and prints (or writes) a human-readable balance summary; the statistics schema is versioned and shared, not duplicated.
- **Tests.** Pure aggregation, determinism and the config-driven arena are covered by unit tests; no wall-clock/IO leaks into the pure core.
- **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
- **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**
## Constraints

- **Determinism (preserve AH-0MUY08XLD009K4W4 AC5).** Every run derives from a
  seed; no wall clock; the batch report is reproducible byte-for-byte.
- **Dev/eval only.** No production runtime impact and no addition to the
  shipped gameplay path; `src/ai/eval/` stays pure (no I/O, no wall clock);
  filesystem work stays in the Node shell (`scripts/evaluate.mjs`).
- **Single source of truth.** The arena must consume the shared config
  loaders (`src/core/configStore.ts` / `enemyConfig.ts` /
  `difficultySequencer.ts`), never a second copy of enemy or ship stats.
- **Gym↔game parity.** The arena is a dev tool (like the gyms); any shared
  gameplay behaviour it exercises must come from the shared core
  (`src/scenes/core/`, `src/utils/movementModel.ts`), never a divergent copy.
- **No PII.** Reuse the existing telemetry schema and redaction policy.
- **Bounded resources.** Hundreds of runs must not exhaust memory; keep the
  per-run footprint small and stream/aggregate incrementally where possible.

## Existing state

- `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` — deterministic headless arena; hardcoded
  `['scout','diver','phaser']`, fixed `ENEMY_FIRE_INTERVAL_TICKS`,
  `HOSTILE_RADIUS`, and `SHIP_CONFIG`; not config-driven.
- `src/ai/eval/metrics.ts` — `MetricPoint`/`MetricAggregate` with score,
  survival, minerals-per-minute, power-ups, enemies/asteroids destroyed,
  avoidable hits, input cadence, dodge rate; **no per-upgrade or per-archetype
  breakdown and no percentile distribution**.
- `src/ai/eval/engine.ts` / `cli.ts` / `report.ts` — single/A-B evaluation over
  a small seed list (`--seeds N`, default 3); reports stored as JSON/JSONL.
- `scripts/evaluate.mjs` — Node shell (Vite SSR module loader, file I/O).
- `docs/EVALUATION.md` — documents the existing harness.
- `src/data/*.csv` + `src/core/configStore.ts` — the real, editable balance
  data and its loader.
- Telemetry already emits `enemy_killed {archetype,x,y}`, `pickup {kind,id}`,
  `mineral_collected {total}`, `choice_selected {index,id}`, `wave_*`,
  `level_cleared`.

## Desired change

Turn the eval harness into an automated-balancing framework:

1. Make the headless arena **config-driven** from the real balance data.
2. Add a **batch runner** for hundreds of deterministic games.
3. Extend the metric layer with the **full balance-statistics schema** and
   distribution summaries (per-upgrade, per-archetype, wave reached, etc.).
4. Emit **JSON + human-readable** balance reports; version the schema so human
   and periodic-validation consumers can share it.
5. Document how to run a batch and interpret the report; cover it with tests.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` — make the arena consume real enemy/ship/wave data.
- `src/ai/eval/metrics.ts` — add balance-statistics extraction + distributions.
- `src/ai/eval/types.ts` — extend statistics/report types (versioned schema).
- `src/ai/eval/report.ts` — include the new statistics and batch summary.
- `src/ai/eval/engine.ts` — batch runner over many games/seeds.
- `src/ai/eval/cli.ts` and `scripts/evaluate.mjs` — CLI flags for batch size,
  statistics output and report.
- `src/ai/eval/index.ts` — public surface for the shared statistics schema.
- `src/core/configStore.ts` / `src/core/enemyConfig.ts` /
  `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` — consumed as the single source of truth.
- `src/ai/eval/*.test.ts` — tests for aggregation, determinism, config-driven
  behaviour.
- `docs/EVALUATION.md` (and/or a new `docs/BALANCING.md`) — how to run a batch
  and read the report.

## Risks, assumptions and mitigations

- **Assumption:** the "reasonably accurate human-like" bot is the `competent`
  policy; the batch runner defaults to it.
- **Assumption:** "hundreds of games" means roughly 100–1000 deterministic
  runs (seeds × policies) per batch.
- **Fidelity risk:** the headless arena is a simplification, so bot balance
  stats may not match the shipped game. *Mitigation:* make it config-driven,
  document the fidelity boundary, and pair it with the human-play statistics
  and periodic human-experience validation items below.
- **Environment risk:** loading CSV-backed config under Node/Vite SSR may need
  verification. *Mitigation:* prototype config loading first (spike within the
  item) before building the statistics layer on top.
- **Scope-creep risk:** human-play collection and periodic human-experience
  validation are **separate work items** (below) — do not fold them into this
  epic. Any further opportunities get their own linked item.

## Related work

- **Same-seed evaluation harness: metrics, A/B, side-by-side** (AH-0MUY08XLD009K4W4) — the foundation this builds on.
- **Dev recording, analysis and replay/ghost tooling** (AH-0MUY08W7Y004GATZ) — recording/analysis path reused for human stats.
- **Telemetry: per-tick integration with no-op contract** (AH-0MUZQEDW9002KHRN) and the telemetry framework (AH-0MUY08VJ9006BHJO).
- **Integrate enemy classification into wave generation and balance tooling** (AH-0MV29XQ0H009P9WP) — balance-rule consumer.
- **Tune enemy balance: reduce scout durability and tank firing** (AH-0MULW9HNC001GVCY) — the manual pass this automates.
- **Collect balance statistics from human player games (dev mode only)** (AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN) — shares the statistics schema.
- **Periodically validate the human experience against the intended experience** (AH-0MV7WVHU0000U775) — depends on this epic.
- **Reduce bullet speed of enemies** (AH-0MUWZ5GST003NMFQ) — a completed tuning pass on `enemy-configs.csv` (bulletSpeed/lifetime) that this framework would measure instead of eyeballing.
- **Write tests for new game scenes and systems** (AH-0MU732AJW005RTG1) — precedent for the test expectations on the new stats layer.
- Docs: `docs/EVALUATION.md`, `docs/TELEMETRY.md`, `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md`, `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `README.md`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- **Q1 — Integration/scope.** How should this relate to the existing same-seed harness?
  - **Answer (operator):** A — extend the existing harness (`src/ai/eval/`, `scripts/evaluate.mjs`, `docs/EVALUATION.md`) with a batch/statistics layer. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2 — Fidelity / what gets simulated.** What should the simulation actually run?
  - **Answer (operator):** A — extend the existing headless arena to be config-driven from `enemy-configs.csv`, `difficulty-curves.csv` and `ship-config.csv`, so tuning edits are measurable. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3 — Statistics and output.** Which statistic set/format?
  - **Answer (operator):** A — full stats (minerals, per-upgrade choice counts, per-archetype kills, wave/level reached, survival-time distribution, avoidable hits) as per-seed + aggregate distributions, output as JSON artifacts and a human-readable report. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q4 — Human player data.** Could the same data be collected from human player games?
  - **Answer (operator):** Yes — create a **high-priority** work item to collect the same data in human player games, **dev mode only**. Created as **Collect balance statistics from human player games (dev mode only)** (AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN). Source: interactive reply.
- **Q5 — Periodic human-experience validation.** Should there be a check against the intended experience?
  - **Answer (operator):** Yes — create another work item, **dependent on both** this framework and the human-play stats item, to periodically validate the human experience against the intended experience. Created as **Periodically validate the human experience against the intended experience** (AH-0MV7WVHU0000U775), with dependency edges to AH-0MV1DLUZ8009OCJW and AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN. Source: interactive reply.

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUCST4M7008O9CX** – Pluggable power-up choice strategy and permanent-effect support (completed)
- **AH-0MUXYOV4C008MV0L** – Demo bot movement goals: minerals > power-ups > enemies > asteroids (completed)

# Balance statistics schema and pure aggregation

## Target outcome
A versioned, shared balance-statistics schema (per-run + aggregate, with distribution summaries including median) extracted purely from the existing telemetry record stream, so bot and human measurements are directly comparable and downstream consumers (AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN, AH-0MV7WVHU0000U775) can import one schema instead of duplicating it.

## Context
The metric layer (`src/ai/eval/metrics.ts`) currently aggregates score/survival/minerals but no per-upgrade or per-archetype breakdown and no percentile/median distribution. This feature extends it with the full balance-statistics schema demanded by the epic AC3/AC4/AC5. Pure core only: no I/O, no wall clock.

## Acceptance Criteria
- New `BalanceStatistics` types (`BalanceRunStats` per-run, `BalanceAggregate` with `DistributionStats` containing count, mean, median, min, max, std-dev) are defined in `src/ai/eval/types.ts` and exported from `src/ai/eval/index.ts` with a versioned schema constant `BALANCE_STATISTICS_SCHEMA_VERSION`.
- `extractBalanceStats(records)` is a pure function over the telemetry record stream deriving: minerals collected, upgrades selected per choice/upgrade id, enemies killed per archetype, asteroids destroyed, power-ups collected, avoidable hits, survival time, and wave/level reached.
- `aggregateBalanceStats(points)` returns distribution summaries (count, mean, median, min, max, std-dev) per metric; median correctness verified in tests.
- Unit tests cover extraction from a synthetic record stream, aggregation incl. median/percentile correctness, empty series, and determinism; tests assert the pure core performs no I/O and never reads the wall clock.
- The schema is versioned and shared (exported), not duplicated in any sibling module.

- **Covers epic AC3:** **Full balance statistics.** The report captures, per run and aggregated, at minimum: minerals collected, upgrades selected (per upgrade/choice id), enemies killed **per archetype**, asteroids destroyed, power-ups collected, avoidable hits, survival time, and wave/level reached — with distribution summaries (count, mean, median, min, max, std-dev) across games.
- **Covers epic AC5:** **Tests.** Pure aggregation, determinism and the config-driven arena are covered by unit tests; no wall-clock/IO leaks into the pure core.
## Minimal implementation
1. Extend `src/ai/eval/types.ts` with balance-statistics types and `BALANCE_STATISTICS_SCHEMA_VERSION`.
2. Add `extractBalanceStats` / `aggregateBalanceStats` (and distribution helper incl. median) to `src/ai/eval/metrics.ts`.
3. Export the new schema from `src/ai/eval/index.ts`.
4. Add `balanceStats.test.ts` (unit tests listed above); update `metrics.test.ts` if interfaces shift.

## Key Files
- `src/ai/eval/types.ts`
- `src/ai/eval/metrics.ts`
- `src/ai/eval/index.ts`
- `src/ai/eval/balanceStats.test.ts`

## Definition of done
All ACs pass; schema exported and versioned; tests green; no wall-clock/IO in the pure core.

# Config-driven headless arena

## Target outcome
The deterministic headless arena (`src/ai/eval/arena.ts`) consumes the real balance data (enemy configs, ship config, difficulty curves) through the shared config loaders instead of the hardcoded `['scout','diver','phaser']`, fixed fire cadence and fixed ship config, so a CSV edit measurably changes simulated outcomes (epic AC1).

## Context
The arena currently hardcodes `ENEMY_FIRE_INTERVAL_TICKS`, `HOSTILE_RADIUS`, `SHIP_CONFIG` and the archetype list. Verification needed: loading CSV-backed config under Node/Vite SSR (the dev path uses `fetch`/`/api/csv`, the Node shell must use the bundled/defaults or an SSR-safe loader — prototype first). Single source of truth: arena consumes `src/core/configStore.ts` / `enemyConfig.ts` / `difficultySequencer.ts` loaders; never a divergent copy of enemy or ship stats.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The arena accepts a resolved balance-config (enemy configs, ship config, difficulty curves) via the existing config loaders (`loadAllEnemyConfigs`, `loadShipConfig`, `loadDifficultyCurves`) with no hardcoded archetype list or duplicated stats.
- A test demonstrates that changing a CSV-backed value (e.g. enemy `health` or `shotProbability`/`fireInterval`) changes the simulated outcome for the same seed.
- The arena translates the shared enemy/ship/wave configs into its spawn reservoir and hostile behaviour using the shared config types.
- Determinism preserved: same seed + config + policy → byte-identical records (epic AC5 preserved from AH-0MUY08XLD009K4W4 AC5).
- SSR config loading under `scripts/evaluate.mjs` is verified (spike) and either wired or explicitly documented as a limitation with a fallback to defaults.

- **Covers epic AC1:** **Config-driven simulation.** A headless run consumes the real balance data (`src/data/enemy-configs.csv`, `src/data/ship-config.csv`, `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` and/or the shared wave sequencer) through the existing config loaders, with no divergent copy of enemy/ship/wave stats. A test demonstrates that changing a CSV value changes the simulated outcome (e.g. enemy health/`shotProbability`).
- **Covers epic AC5:** **Tests.** Pure aggregation, determinism and the config-driven arena are covered by unit tests; no wall-clock/IO leaks into the pure core.
## Minimal implementation
1. Extend `ArenaConfig` to accept a resolved balance config sourced from the shared loaders.
2. Replace the hardcoded constants in `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` with config-driven values.
3. Add a config resolver in the eval layer wired to `src/core/configStore.ts` / `enemyConfig.ts` / `difficultySequencer.ts`.
4. Add the CSV-value-change test and a determinism test in `src/ai/eval/arena.test.ts`.

## Key Files
- `src/ai/eval/arena.ts`
- `src/ai/eval/arena.test.ts`
- `src/ai/eval/types.ts`
- `src/ai/eval/policies.ts`
- `src/core/configStore.ts`
- `src/core/enemyConfig.ts`
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts`
- `scripts/evaluate.mjs`

## Definition of done
Arena is config-driven, CSV-edit test passes, determinism held, SSR loading path verified or limited with documented fallback.

# Deterministic batch runner and config store integration

## Target outcome
A batch runner that runs at least ~100 deterministic bot games (seeds x policy) in one documented invocation, in practical time on a dev machine, emitting raw telemetry plus an aggregated report; same seed + config + policy yields a byte-identical report (epic AC2).

## Context
The existing engine runs single/A-B over a small seed list (default 3). This feature adds a batch mode that sweeps many seeds x policies and aggregates balance statistics incrementally (bounded memory), without disturbing the existing single/A-B paths.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A `runBatch` operation (in `src/ai/eval/engine.ts`) runs >= ~100 deterministic games (seeds x policies, default policy `competent`) in one invocation and completes in a practical time on a dev machine.
- The batch consumes the real balance data via the shared config loaders (config-driven arena, in scope of the sibling feature) so a CSV edit changes batch results.
- Memory stays bounded: per-run telemetry is streamed/aggregated incrementally rather than retaining every run in memory.
- Same seed + config + policy → byte-identical aggregated report (reproducibility preserved).
- Unit tests cover batch size handling, determinism, incremental aggregation equivalence, and memory-bounded aggregation.

- **Covers epic AC2:** **Batch runner.** A documented command runs at least ~100 deterministic bot games (seeds × policy) in one invocation and completes in a practical time on a dev machine, emitting raw telemetry plus an aggregated report. Same seed + config + policy yields a byte-identical report.
## Minimal implementation
1. Add `runBatch` to `src/ai/eval/engine.ts` building on the config-driven arena.
2. Aggregate balance statistics incrementally using the statistics layer.
3. Export batch types/report surface from `src/ai/eval/index.ts`.
4. Add `src/ai/eval/engine.test.ts` / batch tests; ensure no wall-clock or I/O in the pure core (Node shell does file work).

## Key Files
- `src/ai/eval/engine.ts`
- `src/ai/eval/engine.test.ts`
- `src/ai/eval/types.ts`
- `src/ai/eval/report.ts`
- `src/ai/eval/index.ts`

## Definition of done
Batch of ~100 games runs repeatedly byte-identical; tests green; existing single/A-B behaviour unchanged.

# Versioned balance report and CLI batch flags

## Target outcome
The batch writes stable, versioned JSON artifacts and prints/writes a human-readable balance summary; the statistics schema is versioned and shared, not duplicated (epic AC4).

## Context
Current reports (`src/ai/eval/report.ts`) cover single/A-B evaluation with `EVAL_DATASET_VERSION`. This feature adds the balance-batch report kind, the CLI flags (`scripts/evaluate.mjs` / `src/ai/eval/cli.ts`) for batch size, policy selection and output, and the human-readable summary formatter.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A versioned `BalanceReport` (JSON artifact) is produced per batch with stable key order and deterministic serialisation (byte-identical for same inputs).
- A human-readable balance summary is printed/written covering, at minimum: minerals, upgrades per choice id, kills per archetype, asteroids destroyed, power-ups collected, avoidable hits, survival time, wave/level reached — with distribution summaries (count, mean, median, min, max, std-dev).
- `scripts/evaluate.mjs` (and `src/ai/eval/cli.ts`) accept batch flags (e.g. batch size / number of games, policy, output dir) and write the JSON + human-readable artifacts plus raw telemetry JSONL.
- The statistics schema version is exported/shared from `src/ai/eval/index.ts`, not duplicated by any consumer.
- Tests cover report serialisation stability, formatter content, and CLI flag parsing.

- **Covers epic AC4:** **Human-readable + machine-readable output.** The batch writes stable JSON artifacts and prints (or writes) a human-readable balance summary; the statistics schema is versioned and shared, not duplicated.
## Minimal implementation
1. Extend `src/ai/eval/types.ts` + `report.ts` with the balance-batch report kind and schema version.
2. Add a human-readable balance summary formatter to `report.ts`.
3. Extend `src/ai/eval/cli.ts` and `scripts/evaluate.mjs` with batch flags and artifact writing.
4. Add unit tests (`report.test.ts`, `cli.test.ts`, `evaluate-args.test.ts`).

## Key Files
- `src/ai/eval/report.ts`
- `src/ai/eval/types.ts`
- `src/ai/eval/cli.ts`
- `scripts/evaluate.mjs`
- `src/ai/eval/report.test.ts`

## Definition of done
Batch CLI available; JSON + human-readable reports written; schema versioned/shared; tests green.

# Acceptance verification and full suite

## Target outcome
Verify the complete epic end-to-end: a real batch of ~100 games runs byte-identical, a CSV edit changes the report, and the full project test suite passes with the new changes (epic AC7 + verification of AC1/AC2/AC5).

## Context
Per the workflow, no work item reaches `in_review` until all tests pass and acceptance criteria are satisfied. This task closes the loop: demonstrate the framework on the real balance data and run the full suite, triaging any failures before the parent advances.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A documented batch of at least 100 deterministic games is executed against the real balance data files and produces JSON + human-readable reports.
- Re-running the batch with the same seed + config + policy yields a byte-identical report.
- Editing a balance value in the CSV (e.g. enemy health or shotProbability) changes the batch report outcome.
- The full project test suite passes with the new changes (epic AC7); any failures are triaged per project policy before `in_review`.
- Acceptance-criteria coverage is confirmed and recorded (per AC traceability), so the parent epic can be advanced.

- **Covers epic AC7:** **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**
## Minimal implementation
1. Run the batch CLI on the real data; capture artifacts as evidence.
2. Re-run and diff to confirm byte-identical output.
3. Edit a CSV value; re-run; confirm the report changed; revert.
4. Run the full test suite (via the test skill) and triage any failures.
5. Record evidence and AC mapping in a comment on this item and the parent.

## Key Files
- `scripts/evaluate.mjs`
- `src/ai/eval/*.ts`
- `src/data/enemy-configs.csv`
- `src/data/ship-config.csv`

# Shared bullet-shape rendering seam

Child of AH-0MV2K5SR0005RTTE (Variety in weapon graphics). The data-driven rendering seam that lets each weapon id and enemy archetype resolve its own code-drawn projectile shape(s), VFX config and feel, consumed identically by `PlayerBullet` and `bulletUtils` in the game and every gym. Most weapon children depend on this.

## Goal (user story)

As a developer, I want one shared, parity-safe shape resolver so per-weapon and per-archetype bullet visuals live in a single seam the game and every gym consume identically.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. 1. **Distinct in-flight identity.** The shared bullet-shape seam resolves a distinct code-drawn projectile shape and/or per-shot VFX for each weapon id and enemy archetype, differing from every other entry; the doc/roster test asserts catalogue-wide uniqueness (Parity §5.1).
2. A shape resolver (data-driven) exists that draws a shape into a Phaser `Graphics` context from visual metadata (shape kind + params), replaces `PlayerBullet._draw`'s fixed filled circle and `createBullet`'s fixed `fillCircle`, and supports at least: disc, line/beam, teardrop/streak, missile, ring, shell, jagged bolt.

Child of AH-0MV2K5SR0005RTTE (Variety in weapon graphics). Visuals-only: gives the Boss attack a distinct in-flight projectile look, per-shot VFX and fire/impact SFX through the shared bullet-shape seam, gated by its existing fire behaviour.

## Goal (user story)

As a player facing enemy fire, I want the Boss's projectiles to look like they belong to that enemy — an intense desperation volley with bright tracer accents — so I can parse the bullet field and react.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The Boss attack renders via the shared seam with a distinct code-drawn signature — an intense desperation volley with bright tracer accents — differing from every other enemy archetype; the doc/roster test asserts catalogue-wide uniqueness.
2. Fire VFX / launch cue and any in-flight trail for the Boss attack are added through the shared combat-core spawn path as cheap Graphics primitives.
3. Distinct impact VFX + hit SFX play when a Boss projectile hits (or is destroyed), routed through the shared impact path so game and gyms behave identically.
4. Fire/impact SFX: existing `playWeaponFireSound` cue reused (already present) and existing per-enemy impact cue reused where present, recorded in the audio cue manifest.
5. **Gym↔game parity.** Every change lands once in shared core/entities/utils and is consumed by `PlayScene` and the GymBoss gym; the duplicate-body guard and gym-parity assertions pass. Firing logic, speeds, intervals and patterns are unchanged.
6. Full test suite passes, including per-archetype visual/audio tests and updated graphics command-buffer tests.

## Key Files

- `src/entities/bulletUtils.ts` — per-archetype shape seam used by every enemy class
- `src/entities/Boss.ts` — the Boss attack's bullet creation
- `src/audio/effects.ts` + `src/audio/cueManifest.ts` — fire/impact cues
- `src/vfx/` — Boss muzzle/trail/impact module(s)
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` / `CombatScene.ts` — shared spawn/impact hooks
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` + `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts` — parity adoption

## Dependencies

- Parent: AH-0MV2K5SR0005RTTE
- Shared bullet-shape rendering seam (prerequisite child)

## Scope guard

Visuals/feel only. Firing behaviour, speeds, intervals, patterns and balance are unchanged; any change discovered while adding feel is filed separately (`related-to:AH-0MV2K5SR0005RTTE`).

# Documentation: per-weapon visuals & audio cues

Child of AH-0MV2K5SR0005RTTE (Variety in weapon graphics). Updates the documentation to reflect the new per-weapon/per-archetype projectile visuals, VFX, feel and SFX cues.

## Goal (user story)

As a developer or designer, I want the README, the Game Design Document, the enemy design docs and the audio cue manifest to describe each weapon/attack's new visual identity, so the roster stays documented and the audio pipeline stays complete.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. README reflects the new per-weapon projectile visuals and per-weapon feel, consistent with the code-drawn neon aesthetic.
2. The Game Design Document's weapon/enemy sections describe each weapon/attack's distinct in-flight look, VFX and SFX.
3. `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §5.1 parity section and per-enemy documentation describe each archetype's projectile identity and confirm the parity rule.
4. New SFX cues are recorded in the audio cue manifest (`src/audio/cueManifest.ts` + audio cue documentation), matching the baked ToneForge pipeline.
5. Documentation-only change: no production behaviour, visuals or audio modified by this child; docs-guard tests pass.

## Key Files

- `README.md`
- `docs/Game Design Document.md`
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (parity §5.1)
- `src/audio/cueManifest.ts` + audio cue documentation

## Dependencies

- Parent: AH-0MV2K5SR0005RTTE
- Created last, after the weapon/attack children land (documents their visuals).

Documentation only.
